gate: practical block-rate OPL kernel against the exact kernel, perceptual metrics

method.exact_reference: opl-kernel.h at 49,716 Hz, bit exact against Nuked-OPL3
method.candidate: opl-practical.h at 49,169.92 Hz, 48-frame blocks, block-rate envelope and LFO, writes applied at block boundaries
method.lead: how early a write takes effect: its time minus the start of the block that applies it, over every write and over the writes that key a note
method.envelope: RMS per 20 ms window in dBFS at each signal's own rate, each exact window compared with the range the practical envelope spans over the neighbouring three windows; correlation, mean and max absolute dB difference over windows above -60 dBFS; onset skew from the first sample above -40 dBFS after silence
method.spectrum: Hann 125 ms spectra 150 ms into every note of a single-voice scenario; peaks within 48 dB of the strongest are harmonics of the note when within 20 Hz of a multiple of its frequency. Harmonics to 15 kHz and within 30 dB of the strongest are graded for level one by one; all other peaks (aliases fold around each rate's own Nyquist frequency, so they cannot coincide) by their total energy; third-octave bands for the smoothed shape; the pitch from the strongest peak up to the lower Nyquist frequency. In scenarios that hold their notes at a constant level the exact kernel's window is first compared with its own windows 150 and 300 ms later: where it fails the partial thresholds against itself (strong feedback under a loud modulator is not periodic) partials and pitch are not graded, bands and inharmonic peaks are. Mixes get one check per loud stretch, for the 8-15 kHz balance only

not_established: No Falcon or DSP was involved; this scores the host reference of the practical kernel
Perceptual thresholds are engineering targets, not listening-test results
